subject: Duplicate badge scans across kiosks — idempotency & merge policy
messages:
From: ScanRight Events <ops@scanright.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenleafmarketing.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Duplicate badge scans across kiosks — CSV export attached

Hi team,

During this morning's pass over the live ingest we identified ~420 rows where the same badge ID shows up with different hashed emails and slightly different phone numbers across two kiosks (B12 and B14). We've attached the raw export (SF_Expo_2027_badge_duplicates_0527.csv) and a short scanner log showing timestamps and scanner IDs (scanner-log-b12-b14-20270527.txt).

Quick summary:
- Most duplicates are within a 5-10 minute window between kiosk B12 and B14.
- ~18% of duplicates have no email field — only name + phone.
- A handful (21 rows) seem like scanning glitches: same badge_id but different capture timestamps that are implausible (same person scanned simultaneously).

Question for Redwood: what idempotency / dedupe policy should we apply before pushing to HubSpot? Options we can implement upstream in the export:
1) retain-first: keep earliest timestamped row and drop subsequent rows,
2) merge-on-hashed_email: merge rows that share the same hashed_email even if badge_id differs,
3) hold-for-manual-review: flag ambiguous rows and send to a CS queue for manual resolution.

We can include scanner_id and raw_image_ref for any rows you want held for manual review. Blocking action: we will not push an automated update to HubSpot until we get direction on dedupe rules (to avoid overwriting consent flags).

Attached: SF_Expo_2027_badge_duplicates_0527.csv (sample), scanner-log-b12-b14-20270527.txt

—Alex (ops@scanright.io)
ScanRight Events — Onsite Capture & Kiosk Ops
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: ScanRight Events <ops@scanright.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Duplicate badge scans across kiosks — CSV export attached

Thanks Alex — good catch and appreciate the sample. Quick thoughts before we decide:

- Priority: avoid creating duplicate contact records in HubSpot while preserving captured consent. If a second scan has stronger consent (filled form vs passive badge), we should keep the consent-rich record.
- Proposed temporary policy (for this event only):
  * If hashed_email present in any row for a badge_id, merge to that hashed_email as canonical.
  * Otherwise, apply retain-first (earliest timestamp wins) but tag the record with source=badge-batch and add tag=ambiguous-merge if phone/name conflict exists.
  * Any row missing email but with scanner-image_ref -> send to manual review queue.

Can you confirm whether your export can add a column 'scanner_image_ref' and also 'scanner_id' and 'raw_capture_ts' so we can route ambiguous rows to Ops? Also confirm that pushing a merged update will not strip an existing 'consent_form_signed' property in HubSpot if the newer row lacks it.

Lauren / Ben — any objections? If not, I suggest ScanRight proceed with a corrected export and we’ll implement a lightweight merge script in Redwood Optimize to do the merge-on-hashed_email + retain-first with tagging.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head, Field Capture Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, ScanRight Events <ops@scanright.io>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Duplicate badge scans across kiosks — CSV export attached

Adding a couple of specifics from the event ops / privacy side. I pulled a small sample and pasted below (lines redacted for PII):

Sample rows (columns: badge_id, raw_capture_ts, scanner_id, hashed_email, phone_last4, consent_text):
- 75012, 2027-05-26T14:12:05Z, B12, 3f8a9b..., 4321, "Opted in: I agree to receive follow-ups from Redwood and sponsors"
- 75012, 2027-05-26T14:15:30Z, B14, (blank), 4321, "Badge only capture: no explicit opt-in"
- 86433, 2027-05-26T15:02:01Z, B14, f1c2d3..., (blank), "Form opt-in: email provided"

From privacy: if one row has explicit form opt-in text, that is stronger evidence of consent than passive badge-only capture. So merging must preserve the strongest consent flag. Implementation notes:

- Merge precedence: form_opt_in > badge_opt_in > no_consent. If there is any conflict, keep the record with strongest consent and set hubspot_property consent_source accordingly.
- Tagging: add a custom property hubspot:merge_review = "ambiguous-merge" for any retain-first merges where key identifiers differ (name/phone/email mismatch). That will route to CS/manual queue.
- Source attribution: keep a provenance array / field (we can store as comma-separated string) like "source_badge:B12,source_badge:B14,source_form:QR" so we don't lose event attribution.

I uploaded a one-pager with the proposed merge rules: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleSharedDriveId (file: ambiguous-merge-rules-draft.md).

If ScanRight can add scanner_image_ref and scanner_id to the rows you re-export, we can implement the merge logic tomorrow and test on a staging HubSpot sandbox before the Monday push.

—Lauren
Director, Field Marketing Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik / Lauren — we can do that.

Plan of action from ScanRight: 
1) Re-export CSV with columns: badge_id, raw_capture_ts, scanner_id, scanner_image_ref, hashed_email, phone_normalized, consent_text, name_normalized.
2) Add a helper column 'possible_duplicate_reason' when badge_id matches but hashed_email differs or phone differs.
3) Hold rows flagged as 'image_review_required' and provide a zipped folder of image refs for manual review.
4) For automated push we will apply 'retain-first' by default unless 'hashed_email' exists in which case we will mark the hashed_email as canonical and combine attributes.

Attached sample lines from scanner-log-b12-b14-20270527.txt for your review (timestamps truncated):
